species.name: Epilobium palustre
species.tip: Slender willowherb of bogs and fens with narrow, nearly untoothed leaves, small pale pink or whitish flowers and a rounded stem covered in short curved hairs.

species.name: Epilobium parviflorum
species.tip: Softly shaggy willowherb of wet places with stalkless, soft-hairy leaves and larger pink flowers than other small ones, with a four-lobed stigma; stem has spreading hairs.

species.name: Epilobium roseum
species.tip: Slender willowherb with distinct leaf stalks, tiny white flowers fading pink, and a club-shaped, unlobed stigma; grows in gardens, shade and waste places.

species.name: Epilobium tetragonum
species.tip: Upright willowherb with a stem bearing four raised lines, narrow stalkless leaves and small pink flowers with a four-lobed stigma; lacks glandular hairs. Common on open, disturbed ground.

species.name: Epipactis helleborine
species.tip: Tall woodland orchid with oval, ribbed, spirally arranged leaves and a one-sided spike of nodding dull green and purple-pink flowers; often grows in shade, in hedgerows and urban spots.

species.name: Equisetum arvense
species.tip: Common weed with separate early pinkish fertile spring stems, then green sterile stems with simple whorled branches; sheaths have teeth, branches solid and ridged.

species.name: Equisetum fluviatile
species.tip: Horsetail of ponds and ditch edges with smooth, hollow, pale green stems with thin sheaths and branches few or none; fertile cones borne at tips of ordinary stems.

species.name: Equisetum palustre
species.tip: Horsetail of damp ground with grooved stems having wide black-edged sheath teeth with a white margin, and branches either absent or whorled; slender and spreading.

species.name: Equisetum sylvaticum
species.tip: Elegant horsetail of damp woodlands with feathery, repeatedly branched whorls that droop; sheaths on main stem are loose and reddish-brown, with fused teeth.

species.name: Equisetum telmateia
species.tip: Very large, robust horsetail of springs and wet banks; pale unbranched fertile stems in spring, later tall white-green stems with many dense, fine whorled branches.

species.name: Eranthis hyemalis
species.tip: Garden escape in woods and parks; yellow cup flowers in mid-winter sitting on a ruff of deeply cut leaves.

species.name: Erica cinerea
species.tip: Bright reddish-purple bells in whorled clusters along the shoots; dry heaths and rocky slopes, flowering earlier than Cross-leaved Heath, which is paler and on wet ground.

species.name: Erica tetralix
species.tip: Pale pink bells in a terminal head and grey downy leaves in whorls of four forming a cross; wet heaths and bogs.

species.name: Erigeron acris
species.tip: Small daisy with thin lilac-purple rays and a yellow disc, hairy erect stem, narrow leaves. Dry grassland, walls and dunes on calcareous ground.

species.name: Erigeron canadensis
species.tip: Tall, bristly, much-branched weed with masses of tiny whitish heads whose rays barely show. Waste ground, pavements and railway land, summer to autumn.

species.name: Erigeron karvinskianus
species.tip: Wall-colonising daisy with white rays turning pink and yellow centres, often with three-lobed leaves. Flowers for months on walls, steps and rocks.

species.name: Eriophorum angustifolium
species.tip: Several nodding white cottony heads per stem in acid bogs and wet moors; leaves keeled and triangular at tip; spreads by runners, not in tussocks.

species.name: Eriophorum vaginatum
species.tip: Single large white cottony head on each stem, forming dense tussocks on wet moorland and bogs; leaves thin and bristle-like; blooms early.

species.name: Erodium cicutarium
species.tip: Pink flowers with five petals and feathery pinnate leaves; fruit forms a long stork's bill; found on dry sandy and coastal soils, unlike the lobed leaves of Geranium.

species.name: Erophila verna
species.tip: Tiny spring annual of walls and dry banks with a rosette of small leaves, leafless stems and white petals split nearly to the base.

species.name: Ervilia hirsuta
species.tip: Slender scrambling vetch with many pairs of narrow leaflets ending in tendrils and tiny pale lilac flowers; pods hairy with two seeds.

species.name: Ervum tetraspermum
species.tip: Like Hairy Tare but flowers slightly larger, pale lilac, one or two together, and the pods hairless with about four seeds.

species.name: Erysimum cheiranthoides
species.tip: Annual of arable fields and waste ground with narrow toothed leaves, small pale yellow flowers and thin four-sided pods pressed up the stem.

species.name: Erysimum cheiri
species.tip: Fragrant yellow to orange-brown flowers on old walls and cliffs; narrow dark green leaves and a woody base distinguish it from other yellow crucifers.

species.name: Erythranthe guttata
species.tip: Streamsides; large bright yellow two-lipped snapdragon-like flowers, often with small red spots in the throat; opposite toothed leaves.

species.name: Eschscholzia californica
species.tip: Garden escape of verges and waste ground with bright orange-yellow, silky four-petalled flowers and blue-green finely divided leaves.

species.name: Euonymus europaeus
species.tip: Shrub with green square-ish twigs, opposite finely toothed leaves and bright pink four-lobed fruits opening to orange seeds; hedges and scrub on chalk and limestone.

species.name: Eupatorium cannabinum
species.tip: Tall plant with flat-topped clusters of tiny pale pink fluffy heads over hairy, palmately lobed opposite leaves. Wet places, fens and ditches, late summer.

species.name: Euphorbia amygdaloides
species.tip: Shady woodland spurge with evergreen, dark, hairy leaves in rosettes and reddish stems; yellow-green bracts form a branched head in spring, unlike the annual field spurges.

species.name: Euphorbia exigua
species.tip: Small slender annual of arable fields and bare ground with very narrow, grass-like leaves tipped with a tiny point; bracts are narrow and crescent-shaped glands have two horns.

species.name: Euphorbia helioscopia
species.tip: Common annual of cultivated land with rounded, finely toothed leaves broadest near the tip and a flat-topped umbel of five rays, like a tiny sun.

species.name: Euphorbia lathyris
species.tip: Tall, blue-green biennial with crossed pairs of long narrow leaves up the stem; garden escape with fat green caper-like fruits.

species.name: Euphorbia peplus
species.tip: Small garden weed with smooth, stalked, blue-green oval leaves and a three-rayed umbel; glands bear long slender horns, unlike toothed Sun Spurge.

species.name: Euphrasia arctica
species.tip: Small semi-parasitic eyebright of northern and western coasts and grassland with whitish to lilac flowers; best identified by habitat, glandular hairs and the leaf shape. Hard to separate from other eyebrights.

species.name: Euphrasia confusa
species.tip: Tufted eyebright of heath and acid grassland, with white or lilac flowers and toothed leaves; very similar to other eyebrights, which need careful examination to separate.

species.name: Euphrasia micrantha
species.tip: Small eyebright of heaths and dry grassland, with tiny pale lilac to whitish flowers, glandular hairs, and slender unbranched or sparsely branched stems.

species.name: Euphrasia nemorosa
species.tip: The commonest eyebright of grassland and heaths, with white or lilac flowers with a yellow spot and purple veins, and sharply toothed, dark-green leaves; no hairs on glands.

species.name: Fagus sylvatica
species.tip: Smooth grey bark, silky hairy edges to young glossy wavy-edged leaves and tiny catkins; tall woodland tree with copper autumn colour.

species.name: Fallopia convolvulus
species.tip: Twining annual with small greenish flowers and heart-shaped leaves, lacking the large trumpet blooms of true bindweeds; arable fields and gardens, with dark, three-angled fruits.

species.name: Festuca filiformis
species.tip: Bristle-leaved fescue of dry acid grassland with fine hair-thin leaves, short awns and a narrow panicle; shoots tufted, distinct from Red Fescue.

species.name: Festuca ovina
species.tip: Dense tussocks of bristle-fine bluish-green leaves on heaths and downs; small panicle with awned spikelets, leaves all rolled at the base.

species.name: Festuca rubra
species.tip: Creeping fescue of lawns and verges with reddish-tinged panicle; leaf sheaths of non-flowering shoots split, distinguishing it from Sheep's-fescue.

species.name: Festuca vivipara
species.tip: Upland tufted fescue whose spikelets turn into small leafy plantlets rather than flowers; tussocky on mountain grassland and rocks.

species.name: Ficaria verna
species.tip: Early spring; glossy heart-shaped leaves; 8 to 12 narrow, shiny yellow petals; often small bulbils where the leaves join the stem.

species.name: Filipendula ulmaria
species.tip: Tall plant of damp places with frothy creamy flower heads, almond scent and divided leaves white-downy beneath; compare Dropwort of dry chalk.

species.name: Filipendula vulgaris
species.tip: Low plant of dry chalk and limestone grassland with fern-like, finely cut leaves and flat heads of creamy flowers, buds tinged pink; much smaller than Meadowsweet.

species.name: Foeniculum vulgare
species.tip: Tall aniseed-scented plant with feathery thread-like leaves and flat yellow umbels, lacking bracts; found on coasts, waste ground and roadsides, unlike any other yellow umbellifer.

species.name: Fragaria ananassa
species.tip: Larger than Wild Strawberry in flower, fruit and leaves; white flowers often with more than five petals; escapes from gardens onto verges and waste ground.

species.name: Fragaria vesca
species.tip: Small creeping plant with three-leaflet leaves, white flowers and tiny red fruit with seeds on the surface; woods, banks. Barren Strawberry has dry fruit and notched petals.

species.name: Frangula alnus
species.tip: Thornless shrub with alternate smooth-edged leaves, straight veins and berries ripening red to black; wet woods and heaths, unlike thorny, toothed-leaved Purging Buckthorn.

species.name: Fraxinus excelsior
species.tip: Tall tree with opposite pinnate leaves, grey furrowed bark and black buds in winter; flowers appear before the leaves, followed by bunches of winged keys.

species.name: Fuchsia magellanica
species.tip: Garden escape shrub, widely used in hedges in the west, with dangling flowers with red tubes and sepals and purple petals; leaves are oval, in whorls or pairs.

species.name: Fumaria muralis
species.tip: Scrambling fumitory of arable and waste ground, with relatively large pink flowers with dark red tips, and stalks that are short compared with Common Fumitory.

species.name: Fumaria officinalis
species.tip: Weedy fumitory with grey-green finely cut leaves and spikes of small pink flowers tipped with dark red-purple; sepals are small and narrower than the corolla.

species.name: Galanthus nivalis
species.tip: Early nodding white flower with three long outer petals and a green-marked inner ring; grey-green flat leaves; woods and churchyards in late winter.

species.name: Galeopsis tetrahit
species.tip: Bristly stem that swells just below each pair of leaves.

species.name: Galinsoga quadriradiata
species.tip: Weed of gardens and arable land with tiny daisies of five short white rays and a yellow centre, opposite leaves, hairy stems. Distinguished from Gallant-soldier by hairier stems.

species.name: Galium album
species.tip: Tall bedstraw of hedges and verges with whorls of narrow leaves, a square smooth stem and frothy clusters of white flowers; flowers larger than those of Lady's Bedstraw.

species.name: Galium aparine
species.tip: Sticky scrambler of hedges and gardens with whorls of narrow leaves, a rough stem and leaves covered in hooked hairs that cling to clothes; flowers tiny greenish-white.

species.name: Galium odoratum
species.tip: Low woodland plant of shady spots, with whorls of narrow-oval leaves and clusters of small white flowers, and a hay-like smell when dried.

species.name: Galium palustre
species.tip: Straggly bedstraw of wet meadows and ditches with whorls of blunt narrow leaves, black when dry, and loose clusters of white flowers; stem is square and smooth.

species.name: Galium saxatile
species.tip: Low, mat-forming bedstraw of acid grass and heaths, with small bristle-tipped leaves in whorls, backward-pointing, and dense clusters of white flowers.

species.name: Galium uliginosum
species.tip: Slender bedstraw of calcareous fens with leaves in whorls with prickles that point forwards and leaf tips with a bristle; stems are rough, with a loose white flower cluster.

species.name: Galium verum
species.tip: Bedstraw of dry grassland and dunes with frothy masses of tiny golden-yellow, honey-scented flowers and narrow whorled leaves with black edges that curl under.

species.name: Gentianella amarella
species.tip: Purple flowers with five petals and a fringe of hairs in the throat, with a tube typically five-lobed; chalk grassland and dunes, flowering late; Field Gentian is four-lobed.

species.name: Geranium columbinum
species.tip: Deep pink flowers on very long stalks; leaves are cut almost to the base into narrow lobes; fruits smooth. Found on dry calcareous grass and rocky slopes.

species.name: Geranium dissectum
species.tip: Small pink flowers with notched petals in pairs on short stalks; deeply cut leaves; sepals have a short point; fruits are hairy but beakless. Common on arable land.

species.name: Geranium endressii
species.tip: Garden escape with fairly large pink flowers veined darker, with a distinct white eye, and glossy deeply cut leaves; roadside and waste ground, mostly in the south-west.

species.name: Geranium lucidum
species.tip: Glossy, rounded, shallowly lobed leaves often tinged red, and small pink flowers with a wrinkled, keeled calyx; grows on walls, rocks and shady banks, especially on limestone.

species.name: Geranium macrorrhizum
species.tip: Garden escape with strongly aromatic, sticky hairy leaves, rounded shallow lobes and magenta-pink flowers with long protruding stamens; naturalised on banks and walls.

species.name: Geranium molle
species.tip: Soft, rounded, shallowly lobed grey-green leaves and pink flowers with deeply notched petals; fruits are smooth and wrinkled; common on lawns, verges and dry grassland.

species.name: Geranium pratense
species.tip: Large violet-blue flowers with dark veins in lush meadows and verges; deeply cut leaves; the largest-flowered wild blue crane's-bill, flowers more open than Wood Crane's-bill.

species.name: Geranium pusillum
species.tip: Tiny pale lilac to pinkish flowers with notched petals, and only five fertile stamens; leaves rounded with shallow lobes; soft hairy on disturbed bare ground.

species.name: Geranium pyrenaicum
species.tip: Mauve-purple flowers in pairs with deeply notched petals, larger than Dove's-foot, and softer leaves; stems have long soft hairs; grows on grassy verges and hedge banks.

species.name: Geranium robertianum
species.tip: Strongly smelling, often red-tinged plant with pinnately divided ferny leaves and small pink flowers with white stripes; shady walls, woods and shingle.

species.name: Geranium rotundifolium
species.tip: Softly hairy plant with round, shallowly lobed leaves and small pink flowers with unnotched petals; sepals have a short point; fruit smooth. Southern hedgebanks and walls.

species.name: Geranium sanguineum
species.tip: Large, bright magenta flowers with notched petals and deeply cut small leaves turning red in autumn; sprawling, on limestone grassland, sand dunes and coastal cliffs.

species.name: Geranium sylvaticum
species.tip: Violet-blue flowers with a whitish centre, more bowl-shaped than Meadow Crane's-bill; tall plant of northern upland meadows, woods and verges with deeply cut leaves.

species.name: Geum rivale
species.tip: Nodding bell-like flowers dull orange-pink with purple-brown sepals; damp woods, meadows, streamsides. Hybridises with Wood Avens, giving intermediate flowers.

species.name: Geum urbanum
species.tip: Upright yellow five-petalled flowers and hooked fruit burrs; lower leaves pinnate with big terminal lobe; shady hedgerows and woods. Flowers face up, unlike Water Avens.

species.name: Glebionis segetum
species.tip: Bright yellow large daisy with greyish, toothed to lobed hairless leaves clasping the stem. Arable fields and waste ground, summer.

species.name: Glechoma hederacea
species.tip: Kidney-shaped, round-toothed leaves on long creeping stems; smells pungent when crushed.

species.name: Glyceria declinata
species.tip: Low, creeping, often muddy-margin grass with a slender raceme and spikelets on short stalks; leaves are bluish-green and the ligule is long.

species.name: Glyceria fluitans
species.tip: Wet-ground grass floating in ponds and ditches with a long, narrow, one-sided raceme of nearly stalkless spikelets; ligule long and pointed.

species.name: Glyceria maxima
species.tip: Very tall water-edge grass making dense stands, with a big pyramidal panicle of small spikelets and broad leaves; shorter ligule than Floating Sweet-grass.

species.name: Glyceria notata
species.tip: Wet-ground sweet-grass with an open panicle of lined spikelets, branches spreading; leaves medium broad and shorter than Reed Sweet-grass.

species.name: Gnaphalium uliginosum
species.tip: Low grey woolly plant with clusters of dull brownish-yellow heads at stem tops, surrounded by leaves. Damp bare ground in tracks, fields and gardens.

species.name: Gymnocarpium dryopteris
species.tip: Delicate creeping fern of shady rocky woods and screes with a pale, triangular frond divided into three roughly equal branches; fronds are held flat.

species.name: Hedera helix
species.tip: Evergreen climber with lobed leaves on creeping stems and unlobed on flowering stems; round green-yellow umbels in autumn feed insects, followed by black berries.

species.name: Helianthemum nummularium
species.tip: Low spreading evergreen with bright yellow, crumpled-petal flowers and opposite narrow oval leaves, white beneath; sunny chalk grassland and rocks.

species.name: Helictochloa pratensis
species.tip: Oat-grass of chalk grassland with stiff, blue-green leaves and few large spikelets with a bent awn; leaves are folded and hairless.

species.name: Helleborus argutifolius
species.tip: Garden escape with leathery evergreen leaves of three spiny-toothed leaflets and pale green cup flowers in winter.

species.name: Helleborus foetidus
species.tip: Evergreen; dark leaves cut into narrow fingers; nodding pale green bells rimmed with purple in late winter.

species.name: Helleborus orientalis
species.tip: Garden escape; nodding cup flowers in late winter and spring, cream, pink or purple; leathery leaves.

species.name: Helleborus viridis
species.tip: Dies down in winter; flat, open green flowers in early spring; leaves cut into toothed fingers; woods on lime.

species.name: Helminthotheca echioides
species.tip: Coarse, bristly plant with warty-based bristles on leaves and yellow dandelion-like heads, bracts heart-shaped and leafy. Verges, field edges and waste ground.

species.name: Helosciadium inundatum
species.tip: Small plant of pond edges and shallow water with thread-like submerged leaves, pinnate upper leaves and tiny umbels of two or three rays.

species.name: Helosciadium nodiflorum
species.tip: Sprawling in shallow water and ditches; pinnate leaves with toothed leaflets like watercress; small white umbels on short stalks opposite the leaves.

species.name: Heracleum mantegazzianum
species.tip: Huge plant to over 3 m with purple-blotched, thick bristly stems and giant umbels and leaves; sap can cause severe blistering, so do not touch. Far larger than Hogweed.

species.name: Heracleum sphondylium
species.tip: Common coarse umbellifer of verges and rough grass with hairy ridged stems and broad lobed leaves; much smaller than Giant Hogweed and often pinkish-white with unequal outer petals.

species.name: Hesperis matronalis
species.tip: Tall garden escape with sweetly scented purple, lilac or white flowers in spring; unlike phlox it has four petals and long thin pods.

species.name: Hieracium sabaudum
species.tip: Leafy hawkweed with many narrow-ish toothed stem leaves and clusters of yellow heads in late summer. Woods, hedgebanks and heathy places; hawkweeds are hard to identify precisely.

species.name: Hieracium umbellatum
species.tip: Leafy hawkweed with many narrow, nearly stalkless leaves up the stem and a flat-topped umbel of yellow heads. Heaths, dry woodland edges and railway banks.

species.name: Hippophae rhamnoides
species.tip: Thorny coastal shrub with narrow silvery leaves and dense bunches of orange berries in autumn; dunes and sea cliffs, sometimes spreading inland.

species.name: Hippuris vulgaris
species.tip: Aquatic plant with erect stems bearing whorls of narrow leaves like tiny pines; flowers are minute and green in leaf axils. Not related to horsetail; grows in shallow still or slow water.

species.name: Hirschfeldia incana
species.tip: Grey-green, bristly plant of roadsides and waste ground with small pale yellow flowers, pods tight against the stem and a lobed lower leaf.

species.name: Holcus lanatus
species.tip: Softly downy, grey-green grass with velvety leaves and sheaths; pinkish-white panicle with spikelets bearing a short hooked awn; ligule short.

species.name: Holcus mollis
species.tip: Similar to Yorkshire-fog but leaves hairless with hairy nodes and creeping rhizomes; spikelet awns stick out clearly beyond the glumes.

species.name: Honckenya peploides
species.tip: Fleshy, yellowish-green creeping plant on shingle and sand, with pairs of thick oval leaves and small greenish-white flowers. Strandline species.

species.name: Hordeum distichon
species.tip: Cultivated cereal with a stiff nodding head of long-awned spikelets, only the central one of each three fertile; leaves broad.

species.name: Hordeum murinum
species.tip: Annual of walls and waysides with a bristly, yellowish-green spike that breaks up; central spikelet of each three is stalkless, laterals stalked.

species.name: Hordeum secalinum
species.tip: Perennial barley of old damp meadows with a narrower, shorter-awned spike than Wall Barley, blue-green leaves and a bristly feel.

species.name: Humulus lupulus
species.tip: Climbing twining plant of hedges with rough lobed leaves and green papery cones on female plants; grows clockwise, flowering summer.

species.name: Huperzia selago
species.tip: Erect, forked tufts of crowded stiff, pointed leaves with yellowish bulbils at tips; no cones; upland heath, rock ledges and mountain grassland.

species.name: Hyacinthoides hispanica
species.tip: Garden escape with broad leaves and upright, stout stem; wide open bells all round the spike, blue-purple, pink or white, with blue pollen, unlike native Bluebell.

species.name: Hyacinthoides non-scripta
species.tip: Native woodland carpet with a nodding, one-sided flower spike of narrow, deep violet-blue bells whose tips curl back and have cream pollen; sweetly scented.

species.name: Hydrocotyle vulgaris
species.tip: Creeping plant of bogs and wet ground with round, shield-like scalloped leaves on long stalks; flowers tiny and hidden beneath. Not related to Navelwort.

species.name: Hylotelephium telephium
species.tip: Fleshy grey-green oval toothed leaves on upright stems, topped by dense flat heads of reddish-purple starry flowers; woodland edges and hedgebanks.

species.name: Hypericum androsaemum
species.tip: Shrubby plant with large paired oval leaves, yellow flowers in small clusters and berry-like fruit that turns from red to black; woods and hedgerows.

species.name: Hypericum calycinum
species.tip: Evergreen garden shrub with big solitary yellow flowers full of stamens; spreads by suckers on banks and waste ground.

species.name: Hypericum hirsutum
species.tip: Softly hairy stem and leaves without translucent dots on leaf edges; woods and hedges, with pale yellow flowers and black-dotted sepals.

species.name: Hypericum humifusum
species.tip: Low sprawling wiry plant with small pale yellow flowers and small leaves with black dots; acid heaths and tracks, shorter than other St John's-worts.

species.name: Hypericum maculatum
species.tip: Stem with four raised lines and few or no translucent dots on leaves; sepals blunt and not pointed; grassland, scrub and woods.

species.name: Hypericum perforatum
species.tip: Stem with two raised lines and leaves full of see-through dots when held to the light; common on grassland, verges and scrub.

species.name: Hypericum pulchrum
species.tip: Slender plant with round stem and red-tinged buds, flowers with red streaks beneath; leaves clasping with transparent dots; heaths and acid grass.

species.name: Hypericum tetrapterum
species.tip: Stem with four narrow wings on the angles and translucent dots on the leaves; wet meadows, ditches and fens.

species.name: Hypochaeris radicata
species.tip: Dandelion-like but with branched, nearly leafless stems bearing small scale-like bracts and a flat rosette of hairy, lobed leaves. Grassland and lawns, summer.

species.name: Ilex aquifolium
species.tip: Evergreen tree or shrub with glossy spiny leaves, though upper leaves are sometimes smooth; small white flowers and red berries on female trees.

species.name: Impatiens glandulifera
species.tip: Very tall annual with pink-purple hooded flowers, whorled leaves with red stems, and exploding seed pods; common on riverbanks, strongly scented.

species.name: Inula conyzae
species.tip: Tall, sticky-hairy, aromatic plant with rather dull yellowish-brown button heads with short rays, and broad woolly leaves. Dry chalk and limestone scrub and banks.

species.name: Iris foetidissima
species.tip: Evergreen iris of woods and scrub, with dull purplish-yellow flowers and a smell of roast beef from crushed leaves; seed pods split to show bright orange-red seeds.

species.name: Iris pseudacorus
species.tip: Tall wetland iris with sword-like leaves and bright yellow flowers; found along ponds, ditches and marshes, and flowers larger than any other yellow wetland plants.

species.name: Isolepis setacea
species.tip: Tiny tufted plant with thread-like stems, a few small brown spikelets clustered at the side, and one longer bract; damp bare ground and paths.

species.name: Jacobaea aquatica
species.tip: Ragwort of wet places with hairless, little-divided leaves and a broad top; yellow rays spread rather than hang down. Ditches, wet meadows and fens.

species.name: Jacobaea erucifolia
species.tip: Ragwort with narrow-lobed leaves white and cottony beneath, and flat-topped yellow heads. Grassy places on chalk and roadsides, mainly south-east England.

species.name: Jacobaea vulgaris
species.tip: Branched ragwort with ragged, deeply cut leaves and flat-topped clusters of yellow daisies. Very common on grassland and waste ground; poisonous to livestock.

species.name: Jasione montana
species.tip: Looks like a scabious but with a rounded blue pom-pom head of fused-based petals and no bracts like a daisy; dry acid grass and cliffs.

species.name: Juglans regia
species.tip: Large tree with aromatic pinnate leaves with 5 to 9 leaflets and long green catkins; planted and self-sown near fruiting trees, with big green-husked nuts.

species.name: Juncus acutiflorus
species.tip: Tall tufted rush of wet pastures with dark, pointed flower heads and hollow cross-partitioned leaves; branches of the inflorescence spread out; tepals are pointed.

species.name: Juncus articulatus
species.tip: Rush of wet ground with flattened or knotty stems and leaves with visible cross-partitions; flowers dark in clusters whose tepals are pointed; fruits glossy and blunt, shorter than similar rushes.

species.name: Juncus bufonius
species.tip: Small spreading annual of wet bare paths and pond edges with slender branched stems and flowers singly along the branches, green tepals with a white edge.

species.name: Juncus bulbosus
species.tip: Weak, slender, often floating rush of acid bogs and pools whose base swells into bulb-like tufts; flowers are tiny, green and clustered in small heads.

species.name: Juncus conglomeratus
species.tip: Green, soft tufted rush with finely ridged stems and an inflorescence appearing from the side, held tight in compact flower clusters; pith is interrupted and stem ridged when dry.

species.name: Juncus effusus
species.tip: Common tufted rush of damp pastures with smooth, glossy, unribbed green stems when fresh and continuous white pith; flower cluster arises low on stem, often loose.

species.name: Juncus gerardii
species.tip: Fine, flat leaves with bristly dark flower heads in saltmarshes; two-ranked leaves and brownish-black tepals; grows in salt-influenced grassland near the coast.

species.name: Juncus inflexus
species.tip: Blue-green, strongly ridged stiff stems with interrupted pith, and flower clusters emerging well below the stem tip; found in wet, heavy clay or calcareous soils.

species.name: Juncus squarrosus
species.tip: Tufted rush with a rosette of stiff, grooved, curved leaves and dark flower spikes; typical of acid moorland, bog and heath, quite unlike other rushes.

species.name: Juncus tenuis
species.tip: Wiry, slender rush of paths and tracks with long leafy bracts overtopping the loose cluster of pale green-brown flowers; naturalised in North American origin.

species.name: Juniperus communis
species.tip: Prickly conifer shrub with needles in threes, each with a white stripe above, and berry-like cones turning blue-black; chalk downs, moors and uplands.

species.name: Kickxia elatine
species.tip: Trailing annual of arable fields with arrow-shaped leaves with two spreading basal lobes; flowers have a purple upper lip and yellow lower lip. Stalks hairless. Compare Round-leaved Fluellen.

species.name: Kickxia spuria
species.tip: Trailing annual of arable fields with rounded to oval leaves lacking basal lobes; flower stalks are hairy and the flowers have a deep purple upper lip and yellow lower lip.

species.name: Knautia arvensis
species.tip: Rounded heads of lilac-blue flowers, outer florets larger, on tall stems; lobed leaves; tall and hairy, unlike Small Scabious; found on dry grassland and verges.

species.name: Koeleria macrantha
species.tip: Dense, shiny, pale spike-like panicle on dry calcareous grassland; leaves bluish with soft hairs at the base and no awns.

species.name: Laburnum anagyroides
species.tip: Small garden tree with trifoliate leaves and long hanging chains of yellow pea flowers; all parts are poisonous; often self-sown.

species.name: Lactuca serriola
species.tip: Tall, greyish lettuce with leaves twisted to face north-south, prickles along the midrib beneath, and small pale yellow heads. Waste ground and walls.

species.name: Lactuca virosa
species.tip: Tall robust lettuce with big undivided, broad leaves held horizontally and small pale yellow heads in a large pyramid. Waste ground, chalk and coasts; purplish stem.

species.name: Lagarosiphon major
species.tip: Submerged plant with leaves spirally arranged, crowded and strongly curled backwards, giving a bottlebrush look; stiff stems, unlike the whorled leaves of Elodea. Garden pond escape.

species.name: Lamium galeobdolon
species.tip: Yellow flowers with reddish streaks on the lower lip; an ancient-woodland indicator.

species.name: Lamium album
species.tip: Looks like a stinging nettle but has white flowers and does not sting.

species.name: Lamium amplexicaule
species.tip: Upper leaves have no stalk and clasp the stem in pairs beneath the flowers.

species.name: Lamium purpureum
species.tip: Upper leaves crowded and tinged purple; an annual of gardens and bare ground.

species.name: Lapsana communis
species.tip: Slender, branched plant with many small pale yellow heads that open only in the morning, and fruits with no hairy parachute. Hedgebanks, walls and waste places.

species.name: Larix decidua
species.tip: Deciduous conifer with soft needles in tufts, bright green in spring; cones small with straight scales and twigs yellowish, unlike Japanese Larch.

species.name: Larix kaempferi
species.tip: Deciduous conifer with blue-green needles, reddish twigs and cones with scales curved back like a rose; widely planted, unlike European Larch.

species.name: Lathyrus latifolius
species.tip: Climber with winged stems, two broad leaflets, tendrils and large bright pink flower clusters; garden escape on rough ground.

species.name: Lathyrus linifolius
species.tip: Slender plant of woods and heaths with no tendrils, pinnate leaves, and flowers turning from crimson to blue-green; stem is winged.

species.name: Lathyrus nissolia
species.tip: Looks like a grass until it flowers: leaves are narrow and unbranched, with small crimson flowers on long stalks, in rough grassland.

species.name: Lathyrus pratensis
species.tip: Yellow pea flowers in short spikes in grassland and verges; paired narrow pointed leaflets with a simple tendril and a pair of arrow-shaped stipules.

species.name: Lemna gibba
species.tip: Floating duckweed whose rounded fronds are swollen and spongy-looking underneath; fronds are bigger and more rounded than Common Duckweed. Flowers are seldom seen.

species.name: Lemna minor
species.tip: The common duckweed of still ponds, with small flat oval single-rooted fronds, three-veined and floating; flowers are rare and very tiny.

species.name: Lemna minuta
species.tip: Tiny non-native duckweed with very small, narrow-oval fronds having one vein, and spreads rapidly on ponds; smaller than Common Duckweed. Flowers are very rare.

species.name: Lemna trisulca
species.tip: Duckweed submerged under the water surface, with translucent, flat, lance-shaped fronds joined in branching crosses, and only reaches surface during flowering.

species.name: Leontodon hispidus
species.tip: Rosette plant with bristly leaves with forked hairs and single yellow dandelion-like heads on unbranched, leafy-scale stalks. Grassland, mostly on chalk and lime.

species.name: Leontodon saxatilis
species.tip: Small, slender plant with hairless or sparsely hairy leaves, drooping buds and small yellow heads that are red-striped beneath. Short grass, lawns and coastal turf.

species.name: Lepidium campestre
species.tip: Hairy plant of dry grassland and field edges with arrow-shaped stem leaves clasping the stem, small cream flowers and rough heart-shaped pods.

species.name: Lepidium coronopus
species.tip: Flat mat on trampled ground and paths with deeply cut leaves and flower clusters opposite the leaves; pods wrinkled, flattened and not notched.

species.name: Lepidium didymum
species.tip: Strong-smelling annual weed with finely divided leaves, tiny flowers and notched twin-lobed pods; upright and finer than Swine-cress.

species.name: Lepidium draba
species.tip: Patch-forming perennial of roadsides with grey downy foliage, arrow-shaped clasping stem leaves and dense domed clusters of white flowers.

species.name: Lepidium heterophyllum
species.tip: Greyish perennial pepperwort of waste ground and walls with violet anthers on white flowers and oval, clasping upper leaves.

species.name: Leucanthemum vulgare
species.tip: Large white daisy with yellow centre on tall stems, and rounded toothed spoon-shaped basal leaves. Common in meadows and verges, summer.

species.name: Leucojum aestivum
species.tip: Taller than Snowdrop with several white bells, each petal tipped green, on one stem; wet meadows and riverbanks in spring, mainly Thames valley and Ireland.

species.name: Leycesteria formosa
species.tip: Shrub with hollow green bamboo-like stems and hanging spikes of white flowers among purple-red bracts, followed by dark berries; garden escape on waste ground.

species.name: Ligustrum vulgare
species.tip: Semi-evergreen shrub with opposite, narrow dark glossy smooth-edged leaves and heavy-scented creamy flower spikes, followed by shiny black berries; on chalk and limestone scrub.

species.name: Linaria purpurea
species.tip: Garden escape on walls and waste ground; tall, grey-green and slender with spikes of small violet-purple spurred flowers. Plants with pink forms occur; Common Toadflax is yellow.

species.name: Linaria vulgaris
species.tip: Spikes of yellow snapdragon-like flowers with an orange patch and long spur; narrow grey-green leaves crowded up the stem. Grassy banks, verges and hedgerows.

species.name: Linum catharticum
species.tip: Slender annual with tiny white four-to-five-petalled flowers and opposite narrow leaves; chalk and limestone grassland, dunes, short turf, unlike cultivated blue Flax.

species.name: Linum radiola
species.tip: Tiny branched annual of damp acid sandy tracks with paired oval leaves and many minute white four-petalled flowers.

species.name: Linum usitatissimum
species.tip: Tall slender annual with bright blue flowers, narrow alternate leaves and rounded seed capsules; relic of cultivation on waste ground and field edges.

species.name: Littorella uniflora
species.tip: Small tufted plant of lake shores with narrow, pointed, quill-like leaves in a low mat; flowers inconspicuous on short stalks. Resembles a tiny plantain but grows on gravelly or muddy margins.

species.name: Lobelia erinus
species.tip: Small blue bedding plant with two-lipped flowers with a white eye, straggling stems and toothed leaves; occasional escape on pavements and walls.

species.name: Lobularia maritima
species.tip: Low, tufted garden escape with grey narrow leaves and masses of small honey-scented white flowers on walls and paving, flowering for months.

species.name: Lolium multiflorum
species.tip: Rye-grass with awns on the spikelets and rolled young leaves, broader and glossier than Perennial Rye-grass; short-lived, sown in leys.

species.name: Lolium perenne
species.tip: Common sown grass with a flat two-rowed spike, spikelets facing the stem edge-on and awnless; young leaves folded, shiny underneath.

species.name: Lonicera japonica
species.tip: Twining semi-evergreen climber with paired, fragrant white flowers ageing yellow, and black berries; rare escape, differing from native Honeysuckle in having hairy shoots.

species.name: Lonicera periclymenum
species.tip: Native twining climber of hedges and woods with pairs of tubular, creamy yellow flowers flushed pink, strongly scented at night; red berries in clusters in autumn.

species.name: Lotus corniculatus
species.tip: Yellow flowers often with orange buds in heads of 2-6; five leaflets, solid stem and pods spreading like a bird's foot.

species.name: Lotus pedunculatus
species.tip: Taller than Common Bird's-foot-trefoil with hollow stems, wetter habitats and heads of 5-12 flowers, blue-green leaflets and flowers reddish in bud.

species.name: Lunaria annua
species.tip: Garden escape with heart-shaped toothed leaves, purple or white flowers and, later, round papery silvery seed discs.

species.name: Luzula campestris
species.tip: Short, early-flowering grass-like plant with hairy leaves and spread-out clusters of dark brown flowers with yellow anthers; lawns and meadows; flowers earlier than other wood-rushes.

species.name: Luzula multiflora
species.tip: Clump-forming and hairy-leaved, with flowers in several dense brown heads on stalks of unequal length; acid grassland and heaths, flowering later than Field Wood-rush.

species.name: Luzula pilosa
species.tip: Woodland species with broad, hairy grass-like leaves and flowers solitary on drooping stalks, then fruits that bend down; the flowers are chestnut brown.

species.name: Luzula sylvatica
species.tip: Large tussock-forming wood-rush with glossy, broad, shiny leaves edged with long hairs; dense brown flower heads in spring; grows in damp, shady woods and on mountain ledges.

species.name: Lycium barbarum
species.tip: Lax, spiny-tipped shrub of hedges and waste ground with narrow grey-green leaves, small purple funnel-shaped flowers and orange-red berries.

species.name: Lycopodium clavatum
species.tip: Creeping clubmoss with leaves bearing a white hair tip and spore cones on slim stalks in pairs; heaths and moors, unlike erect Fir Clubmoss.

species.name: Lycopus europaeus
species.tip: Deeply toothed to lobed leaves; tiny purple-dotted white flowers in tight whorls.

species.name: Lysichiton americanus
species.tip: Large garden escape of wet woods and stream banks with huge, cabbage-like leaves, and a bright yellow hooded spathe appearing in spring; has a skunk-like smell.

species.name: Lysimachia arvensis
species.tip: Low sprawling annual of bare and cultivated ground; small orange-red five-petalled flowers that close in dull weather; opposite unstalked oval leaves dotted beneath.

species.name: Lysimachia europaea
species.tip: Northern woods and moors; a single whorl of shiny leaves at the top of a slender stem with one or two starry white flowers of about seven petals.

species.name: Lysimachia maritima
species.tip: Low fleshy plant of saltmarshes and coastal rocks; small pink flowers with no petals, sitting in the leaf joints; opposite oval leaves.

species.name: Lysimachia minima
species.tip: Minute annual of damp bare sandy or peaty ground, often under 5 cm; tiny pinkish flowers hidden in the leaf joints.

species.name: Lysimachia nemorum
species.tip: Creeping woodland plant with solitary star-like yellow flowers on slender stalks and pointed oval paired leaves; shady woods and streamsides.

species.name: Lysimachia nummularia
species.tip: Trailing mat with rounded paired leaves and large cup-shaped yellow flowers singly in leaf axils; damp grass and riverbanks.

species.name: Lysimachia punctata
species.tip: Garden escape with whorled hairy leaves and whorls of yellow flowers with fringed edges and orange spots; stands upright on verges and waste ground.

species.name: Lysimachia tenella
species.tip: Creeping mats in wet acid ground with tiny round paired leaves and delicate pale pink bell-shaped flowers on long thin stalks.

species.name: Lysimachia vulgaris
species.tip: Tall plant of waterside with paired or whorled lance-shaped leaves and big branched panicle of yellow flowers; riverbanks and fens.

species.name: Lythrum portula
species.tip: Small creeping annual of wet muddy places with opposite spoon-shaped leaves and tiny stalkless flowers in leaf axils; flowers are easily overlooked.

species.name: Lythrum salicaria
species.tip: Tall plant of wet places with leafy spikes of vivid magenta flowers and opposite or whorled narrow leaves, in summer; unlike willowherbs, has six petals.

species.name: Mahonia aquifolium
species.tip: Evergreen shrub with glossy holly-like pinnate leaves and dense upright yellow flower clusters in early spring; later blue-black berries. Planted and naturalised, no spines on stem.

species.name: Malus domestica
species.tip: Cultivated apple escaping from gardens: leaves downy beneath, white flowers flushed pink, large sweet fruit. Wild Crab Apple has hairless leaves and small sour fruit.

species.name: Malus sylvestris
species.tip: Native tree of woods and hedges with blossom white flushed pink; leaves hairless when mature, small sour yellow-green fruit; twigs sometimes spiny. Cultivated Apple has downy leaves.

species.name: Malva moschata
species.tip: Roadside and grassland mallow with large, pale pink flowers with notched petals; the upper leaves are deeply cut into narrow segments, unlike Common Mallow.

species.name: Malva neglecta
species.tip: Low, spreading weed of waste ground with small, pale lilac-white flowers and rounded, shallowly lobed leaves; fruiting stalks bend down and the petals are barely longer than the sepals.

species.name: Malva sylvestris
species.tip: Tall, bushy plant of verges and waste ground, with pink-purple flowers veined darker and five-lobed leaves; petals are much longer than the sepals and are notched.

species.name: Matricaria chamomilla
species.tip: Finely divided feathery leaves smelling sweetly of apples, and small white-rayed daisies with a cone-shaped hollow yellow centre. Arable land and waste ground.

species.name: Matricaria discoidea
species.tip: Greenish-yellow rayless button heads, feathery leaves that smell of pineapple when crushed. Trampled ground, gateways and paths.

species.name: Medicago arabica
species.tip: Clover-like leaves with a dark central blotch and small yellow flowers in clusters of 1-5; coiled spiny pods; lawns and dry ground.

species.name: Medicago lupulina
species.tip: Low yellow clover-like plant with small round flower heads and kidney-shaped black pods, leaflets with a tiny point on the tip.

species.name: Medicago sativa
species.tip: Purple flower clusters in tall oblong spikes with clover-like leaves on field edges; pods coiled like small springs.

species.name: Melampyrum pratense
species.tip: Semi-parasitic annual of woods and heaths with opposite narrow leaves and pale yellow, closed tubular flowers in pairs, all facing one side of the stem.

species.name: Melica uniflora
species.tip: Woodland grass with delicate loose raceme of few brownish-purple spikelets; no awns, sheaths slightly hairy and ligule short with a lobe.

species.name: Melilotus albus
species.tip: Tall plant with long spikes of small white flowers and trifoliate toothed leaves; smells of new hay; waste ground and roadsides.

species.name: Melilotus altissimus
species.tip: Yellow-flowered melilot with hairy, downy pods and wings and keel of equal length; keel equals standard, pods black when ripe.

species.name: Melilotus officinalis
species.tip: Yellow melilot with hairless, transversely ribbed pods that are brown when ripe; wings longer than keel; roadsides and waste ground.

species.name: Mentha aquatica
species.tip: Rounded lilac flower head at the stem tip; strong mint smell.

species.name: Mentha arvensis
species.tip: Flowers only in whorls up the stem; the stem ends in leaves, not flowers.

species.name: Menyanthes trifoliata
species.tip: Wetland plant with three-leaflet leaves and spikes of white to pink fringed star-like flowers; shallow water, bogs and fens in spring.

species.name: Mercurialis annua
species.tip: Weed of gardens and arable land with bright green, shiny toothed leaves; male and female flowers on separate plants, tiny and green, in leaf axils. Stem is branched and brittle.

species.name: Mercurialis perennis
species.tip: Carpeting woodland perennial of ancient woods, unbranched hairy stems with toothed dark green leaves; tiny green flowers in early spring, poisonous and unscented.

species.name: Micranthes stellaris
species.tip: Upland streamsides and wet rocks; rosettes of toothed leaves and starry white flowers with two yellow spots on each petal and red anthers.

species.name: Milium effusum
species.tip: Tall, graceful woodland grass with a large open panicle of drooping branches, small unawned spikelets, broad flat soft leaves and a long ligule.

species.name: Moehringia trinervia
species.tip: Woodland plant with oval leaves showing three clear veins and small white flowers with petals shorter than sepals. Weak straggling stems in shady, damp woods.

species.name: Molinia caerulea
species.tip: Large tussocks on wet heath with a narrow purplish panicle; ligule is a fringe of hairs and the stem has only one node near the base.

species.name: Montia fontana
species.tip: Tiny, pale green, bright, spreading plant of wet springs, flushes and seepages with minute white flowers and opposite spoon-shaped leaves; much smaller than the purslanes.

species.name: Muscari armeniacum
species.tip: Garden escape on verges and waste ground with narrow, floppy leaves and a dense spike of small, rounded blue urn-shaped flowers with a white rim.

species.name: Mycelis muralis
species.tip: Slender, hairless plant with a loose spray of tiny heads of only five yellow florets and leaves with a large terminal lobe. Shady walls and woodland.

species.name: Myosotis arvensis
species.tip: Hairy forget-me-not with small blue flowers and a calyx covered in hooked hairs, with style shorter than calyx. Arable land and open ground.

species.name: Myosotis discolor
species.tip: Tiny flowers that change from cream or yellow to blue as they age, within a coiled spike; calyx with hooked hairs. Dry sandy grassland and fields.

species.name: Myosotis laxa
species.tip: Forget-me-not of wet places with tiny pale blue flowers, with open calyx without hooked hairs, and fruit stalks longer than calyx. Compare Water Forget-me-not.

species.name: Myosotis ramosissima
species.tip: Tiny early-flowering annual with sky-blue flowers on short stalks, and calyx with hooked hairs. Dry open ground, flowering from early spring.

species.name: Myosotis scorpioides
species.tip: Stems rooting in wet places, flowers sky-blue with yellow eye, calyx with short teeth. Stream sides, ditches and marshes; larger flowers than other wet-place forget-me-nots.

species.name: Myosotis secunda
species.tip: Perennial of wet, acidic, upland places, creeping with rooting stems and bright blue flowers; calyx with open lobes in fruit. Streams and flushes.

species.name: Myosotis sylvatica
species.tip: Larger flowers in woods than other forget-me-nots, bright blue with a yellow centre, on hairy stems; calyx with hooked hairs. Woodland and garden escapes.

species.name: Myosurus minimus
species.tip: Tiny plant with grass-like leaves; the fruiting head stretches into a long, thin, mouse-tail spike.

species.name: Myrica gale
species.tip: Fragrant low shrub of wet heaths and bogs with aromatic grey-green leaves and reddish catkins before the leaves appear; crush leaf to smell resin.

species.name: Myriophyllum alterniflorum
species.tip: Submerged plant with feathery whorled leaves, flower spike tip often drooping and flowers alternately arranged; in acid, peaty waters, unlike coarser Spiked Water-milfoil.

species.name: Myriophyllum spicatum
species.tip: Submerged plant with feathery leaves in whorls of four and more than 13 pairs of thread-like segments; erect red-tinged flower spikes in hard, base-rich water.

species.name: Myrrhis odorata
species.tip: Aniseed-scented, softly hairy plant of northern grassy verges with fern-like leaves often marked with white blotches; fruits are large, long and glossy brown.

species.name: Narcissus poeticus
species.tip: Flat white petals around a small yellow cup edged red, fragrant, one flower per stem; late-flowering, in grassland or as an escape.

species.name: Narcissus pseudonarcissus
species.tip: Smaller than garden daffodils with pale yellow twisted petals and a deeper yellow trumpet; grassy woods and meadows in early spring.

species.name: Nardus stricta
species.tip: Wiry, bristly-leaved tussock of acid upland grass with a slim one-sided spike of purplish spikelets; leaves stiff and harsh, bleached in winter.

species.name: Narthecium ossifragum
species.tip: Tufts of flat iris-like leaves and spikes of star-shaped yellow flowers with orange anthers on wet moors and bogs; orange fruit follows.

species.name: Nasturtium microphyllum
species.tip: Water-cress growing in streams with leaves turning bronze-purple in autumn; fruit narrow and in a single row of seeds per segment.

species.name: Nasturtium officinale
species.tip: Edible aquatic plant of streams and ditches with glossy dark pinnate leaves that stay green; fruit seeds in two rows.

species.name: Neottia cordata
species.tip: Tiny orchid of moorland among heather and moss, with one pair of small heart-shaped leaves and a few minute reddish-green flowers; much smaller than Common Twayblade.

species.name: Neottia ovata
species.tip: Orchid of woods, meadows and dunes with just two large oval opposite leaves at mid-stem and a long spike of yellow-green flowers with a forked lip.

species.name: Nigella damascena
species.tip: Garden escape; blue flowers in a ruff of thread-like bracts; swollen, balloon-like seed pods.

species.name: Nuphar lutea
species.tip: Floating oval leaves with notch at base and rounded yellow ball-like flowers held at the surface, smelling of alcohol; ponds, canals and slow rivers.

species.name: Nymphaea alba
species.tip: Large white flowers with many petals and yellow centre floating on round, deeply notched leaves; lakes and ponds, bigger and whiter than any other native water plant.

species.name: Nymphoides peltata
species.tip: Floating plant with small water-lily-like heart-shaped leaves and yellow five-petalled fringed flowers held above water; ponds and slow rivers, not a true water-lily.

species.name: Odontites vernus
species.tip: Branched annual of grassy and disturbed ground with narrow toothed leaves and spikes of small pink-red flowers, with a one-sided flowering spike; stems often reddish.

species.name: Oenanthe crocata
species.tip: Very poisonous plant of ditches and wet places with celery-like glossy leaves, thick hollow stems and rounded umbels; sap turns yellowish-orange when cut.

species.name: Oenothera biennis
species.tip: Tall biennial of sands and waste ground with pale yellow flowers opening at dusk; flowers are smaller than Large-flowered Evening-primrose and sepals are green without red stripes.

species.name: Oenothera glazioviana
species.tip: Tall, robust evening-primrose of dunes and waste ground with big bright yellow flowers, red-based hairs on the stem and red-striped buds, flowers larger than Common Evening-primrose.

species.name: Omalotheca sylvatica
species.tip: Upright, grey-woolly plant with narrow leaves and a spike of small brown-tipped heads in leaf axils. Open heathy ground and tracks.

species.name: Onobrychis viciifolia
species.tip: Dense spikes of pink veined flowers on chalk grassland and verges; leaves pinnate with many narrow leaflets, no tendrils.

species.name: Ononis repens
species.tip: Low, spreading, hairy, sticky plant with pink pea flowers and small toothed trifoliate leaves; unlike Spiny Restharrow it has no spines.

species.name: Onopordum acanthium
species.tip: Huge, silvery-woolly thistle with broad spiny wings on the stem and large purple heads. Waste ground, field edges and roadsides, mainly eastern England.

species.name: Ophioglossum vulgatum
species.tip: Small fern with one oval, undivided green blade and a spore spike rising from its base like a snake tongue; damp meadows and old grassland.

species.name: Ophrys apifera
species.tip: Orchid of calcareous grass and quarries with flowers resembling a bumblebee, pink petals and a brown velvety lip with yellow markings; stems bear a few narrow leaves.

species.name: Orchis mascula
species.tip: Spring orchid of woods and meadows with leaves usually blotched purple-black, a loose spike of magenta flowers and a long spur; smells unpleasantly of tomcat in older flowers.

species.name: Oreopteris limbosperma
species.tip: Tufted fern of hill slopes and acid woods with fronds tapering at both ends and smelling of lemon when crushed; the lowest pinnae are tiny. Has yellow glands beneath.

species.name: Origanum vulgare
species.tip: Loose, branched clusters with purple bracts; smells of oregano.

species.name: Ornithogalum umbellatum
species.tip: Bulb with narrow, grass-like leaves with a white midstripe, and starry white flowers striped green on the back; opens only in sun; garden escape in grass.

species.name: Ornithopus perpusillus
species.tip: Small, hairy annual of sandy heaths with tiny pinkish-white flowers in clusters and feathery pinnate leaves; pods curved like bird claws.

species.name: Orobanche minor
species.tip: Leafless, yellowish-brown parasitic plant with scales rather than leaves, usually on clovers and other legumes; flowers have a purple-tinged tube and curved lip.

species.name: Osmunda regalis
species.tip: Tall fern with twice-pinnate fronds, rounded leaflets, and brown spore clusters at the frond tip; wet woods and bogs, large and distinctive.

species.name: Oxalis acetosella
species.tip: Delicate woodland plant with clover-like, heart-shaped drooping leaflets and nodding white flowers with purple veins on slender stalks; leaves fold at night.

species.name: Oxalis articulata
species.tip: Garden escape with clover-like leaves on hairy stalks from a rhizome and heads of bright pink flowers with darker veins; found on verges and waste ground.

species.name: Oxalis corniculata
species.tip: Creeping weed of paths and gardens with clover-like green or purple leaves and small yellow flowers; stipules are present and the stems root at nodes.

species.name: Oxalis exilis
species.tip: Very small, creeping New Zealand plant of lawns and paths with tiny clover-like leaves and single small yellow flowers; leaves have no purple tinge.

species.name: Oxybasis rubra
species.tip: Fleshy, often red-tinged goosefoot of manure heaps, pond margins and saltmarsh edges with diamond-shaped toothed leaves and dense green flower spikes.

species.name: Papaver dubium
species.tip: Poppy with paler scarlet flowers, hairs pressed against the stem, and a long narrow smooth seed capsule; the capsule is more than twice as long as it is wide.

species.name: Papaver rhoeas
species.tip: Familiar field poppy with bright scarlet petals, often with a dark blotch, spreading hairs on stems and a rounded, smooth seed capsule.

species.name: Papaver somniferum
species.tip: Tall blue-grey poppy of waste ground and gardens, hairless, with large white, pink or mauve flowers often dark at the base and big globe-like seed capsules.

species.name: Parietaria judaica
species.tip: Bushy perennial of walls and rocks with reddish, softly hairy stems and alternate, untoothed oval leaves; tiny clustered green flowers in leaf axils, no stings.

species.name: Parnassia palustris
species.tip: White five-petalled flower with green veins, fan of false stamens, on a stem with single clasping leaf; wet, peaty and calcareous flushes, late summer. Not a grass.

species.name: Parthenocissus quinquefolia
species.tip: Climbing vine with leaves of five leaflets and tendrils with sticky pads, turning scarlet in autumn; garden escape on walls and hedges.

species.name: Pastinaca sativa
species.tip: Only common umbellifer with yellow flowers and simple once-pinnate leaves with broad lobed leaflets; furrowed hairy stems, smelling of parsnip, on calcareous grassland.

species.name: Pedicularis palustris
species.tip: Hairless plant of wet meadows and fens with finely cut, fern-like leaves and clustered pink-red flowers with a toothed hood; stem often branched.

species.name: Pedicularis sylvatica
species.tip: Low plant of damp heaths and moors with finely cut leaves and pink flowers on short stems; calyx is inflated and stems are sprawling, unlike taller Marsh Lousewort.

species.name: Pentaglottis sempervirens
species.tip: Large bristly perennial with bright blue flowers with white centres and big dark green oval leaves. Hedgebanks and roadsides, naturalised from gardens.

species.name: Persicaria amphibia
species.tip: Pink flower spikes are broad and blunt; either floating glossy leaves in ponds and ditches or a hairy land form on damp soil.

species.name: Persicaria hydropiper
species.tip: Slender spikes of small greenish-pink flowers, drooping at the tips and speckled with glands; leaves have a hot peppery taste and wet places are favoured.

species.name: Persicaria lapathifolia
species.tip: Thick, dense, blunt spikes of pale pink to greenish-white flowers, usually nodding; stalks bear glands beneath; leaves often have a dark blotch. Arable fields and damp places.

species.name: Persicaria maculosa
species.tip: Spikes of pink flowers held upright, with stalks lacking glands, and leaves often with a dark blotch; reddish stem joints; common annual in arable land and waste ground.

species.name: Petasites hybridus
species.tip: Early spikes of pale pink flower heads appear before giant, rhubarb-like round leaves. Wet verges and riverbanks.

species.name: Phacelia tanacetifolia
species.tip: Tall annual with feathery deeply cut leaves and dense coiled spikes of lilac-blue flowers with protruding stamens, loved by bees. Sown as green manure and field margins.

species.name: Phalaris arundinacea
species.tip: Tall riverside grass making stands, with a lobed greenish-purple panicle becoming buff; flat, broad, rough-edged leaves and long ligule.

species.name: Phalaris canariensis
species.tip: Birdseed casual with a short, egg-shaped, dense head of pale striped spikelets with winged keels; stem leaves broad and unawned.

species.name: Phegopteris connectilis
species.tip: Fern of damp, shady rocky banks with a triangular, pale green hairy frond with the lowest pair of leaflets bent down and pointing forwards; fronds are held flat.

species.name: Phleum bertolonii
species.tip: Short cylindrical head with short awns and a wedge-shaped, shorter spikelet than Timothy; smaller grass of dry grassland, tapered cylinder.

species.name: Phleum pratense
species.tip: Long, narrow, evenly cylindrical head, soft and pale green; spikelets with short awns, and the stem base is swollen into a bulb.

species.name: Phragmites australis
species.tip: Very tall, reedy grass of fens and margins forming vast stands with purplish silky plumes; ligule is a fringe of hairs and leaves are broad.

species.name: Picea abies
species.tip: Typical Christmas-tree spruce with hanging long cones and four-sided needles that are not sharp; planted widely in forests.

species.name: Picea sitchensis
species.tip: Spruce with sharp, spiky flattened needles, blue-white beneath, and short cones with papery scales; widely planted in wet upland forests.

species.name: Picris hieracioides
species.tip: Tall, bristly plant with unlobed narrow leaves and yellow dandelion-like heads with dark bristly bracts, on branching stems. Dry grassland and banks, mostly on chalk.

species.name: Pilosella aurantiaca
species.tip: Orange-red dandelion-like heads, several to a stem, with black-hairy bracts and hairy rosette leaves. Garden escape on grassy banks, walls and verges.

species.name: Pilosella officinarum
species.tip: Low mat-forming plant with silvery-white, felted leaf undersides and pale lemon, single heads, red-striped beneath. Dry banks, walls and short turf.

species.name: Pimpinella major
species.tip: Taller than Burnet-saxifrage with a hollow, angled stem and undivided, deeply toothed leaflets on upper leaves; flowers white or pinkish, in hedgerows and damp grass.

species.name: Pimpinella saxifraga
species.tip: Slender, wiry plant of dry grassland with round-toothed lower leaflets and finely cut upper leaves; stem is solid, finely ridged and not angled, with no bracts.

species.name: Pinguicula vulgaris
species.tip: Sticky yellow-green rosette of rolled-edge leaves trapping insects, with single violet flower on a leafless stalk; wet moors, bogs and flushes.

species.name: Pinus contorta
species.tip: Pine with paired twisted dark green needles and small prickly cones that stay on the tree; planted on poor wet peaty ground.

species.name: Pinus nigra
species.tip: Tall pine with long, grey-green, twisted needles in pairs and a straight trunk; planted on sandy soils and coasts, unlike Scots Pine.

species.name: Pinus sylvestris
species.tip: Pine with short blue-green paired needles, orange-red upper bark and flat-topped crown with age; native pinewoods and widely planted.

species.name: Plantago coronopus
species.tip: Flat rosette of narrow leaves cut into toothed lobes like antlers, with curved stalks and slender spikes. Coastal turf, sandy and gravelly places; also inland on dry gravel.

species.name: Plantago lanceolata
species.tip: Narrow ribbed leaves in a rosette, and a short dark brown head with a ring of white stamens on a long furrowed stalk. Very common in grassland and lawns.

species.name: Plantago major
species.tip: Broad oval leaves with five to nine strong veins and a long rat-tail spike of tiny greenish flowers. Common on paths, gateways and trampled ground.

species.name: Plantago maritima
species.tip: Rosette of narrow, fleshy, slightly toothed or smooth leaves on salt marshes, sea cliffs and mountain rocks; stiff narrow spikes. Distinguished from Ribwort by its fleshy leaves and coastal habitat.

species.name: Plantago media
species.tip: Broad downy oval leaves pressed flat in a rosette; fragrant lilac-pink stamens in a short head on a long stalk. Calcareous grassland and lawns.

species.name: Platanthera chlorantha
species.tip: Orchid of woods and meadows with two large oval leaves near base and greenish-white flowers with parallel pollen sacks; flowers are larger than Lesser Butterfly-orchid and scented at night.

species.name: Poa angustifolia
species.tip: Meadow-grass with narrow, stiff, rolled blue-green leaves and creeping rhizomes; panicle open and slightly smaller than Smooth Meadow-grass.

species.name: Poa annua
species.tip: Small, pale-green, tufted grass flowering all year; crinkled leaf blades with a boat-shaped tip and a spreading panicle; very common on paths.

species.name: Poa compressa
species.tip: Distinctive for its flat, wiry stems and blue-green leaves; narrow dense panicle, creeping rhizomes, grows on walls and dry ground.

species.name: Poa humilis
species.tip: Meadow-grass similar to Smooth Meadow-grass, with blue-green leaves and slender creeping rhizomes; panicle more open with spreading branches.

species.name: Poa nemoralis
species.tip: Slender woodland meadow-grass with wiry, thin stems and a thin open panicle; leaves narrow and tufted with a very short ligule.

species.name: Poa pratensis
species.tip: Common meadow-grass spreading by rhizomes with smooth sheaths and a short ligule; leaf tips boat-shaped, with twin lines along the leaf blade.

species.name: Poa trivialis
species.tip: Meadow-grass of damp shaded ground with a long pointed ligule and rough sheaths; stoloniferous and light green, with panicle open.

species.name: Polygala serpyllifolia
species.tip: Small, wiry plant with lower leaves opposite, small blue, pink or white flowers; acid heaths and grassland, unlike Common Milkwort, leaves all alternate.

species.name: Polygala vulgaris
species.tip: Low plant with all leaves alternate, narrow, and spikes of small blue, pink or white flowers; chalk and neutral grassland, versus Heath Milkwort.

species.name: Polygonum aviculare
species.tip: Mat-forming, wiry, much-branched annual with tiny flowers in leaf axils, tiny pink-edged green petals, and grey-green small leaves; trampled paths, arable fields and waste ground.

species.name: Polypodium interjectum
species.tip: Evergreen fern on walls, trees and rocks with fronds longest in the middle; sori oval and fronds with finely toothed tips, unlike the other polypody.

species.name: Polypodium vulgare
species.tip: Evergreen rock and tree fern with once-cut fronds having parallel sides and blunt tips; round orange sori; differs from Intermediate Polypody by rounded outline.

species.name: Polypogon viridis
species.tip: Introduced grass of damp places with a dense, green, lobed cylindrical panicle that has no awns; stems often creeping and ligule long.

species.name: Polystichum aculeatum
species.tip: Stiff, glossy dark green fronds with spiny, bristle-tipped pinnules that overlap and are once divided; woods and shaded banks.

species.name: Polystichum setiferum
species.tip: Soft, drooping, twice-cut fronds with bristle-tipped pinnules, thinner than Hard Shield-fern; shaded lanes and woods in the west.

species.name: Populus alba
species.tip: Large suckering tree with leaves that are lobed and maple-like and snowy-white felted beneath; bark is pale with diamond-shaped marks. Catkins appear early spring.

species.name: Populus nigra
species.tip: Rare native tree of floodplains with big burry trunk, drooping branches and triangular, finely toothed hairless leaves; female trees are scarce. Hybrid poplars are far more frequent.

species.name: Populus tremula
species.tip: Poplar with rounded leaves on long flat stalks, so they tremble in even a slight breeze; forms suckering thickets on heaths, woodland edges and in the north.

species.name: Potamogeton berchtoldii
species.tip: Slender submerged pondweed with narrow, translucent, three-veined leaves tapering to a point and flowers held in small short spikes; leaves are broader than in Lesser Pondweed.

species.name: Potamogeton crispus
species.tip: Submerged pondweed with distinctive wavy, finely toothed, crinkled translucent leaves like seaweed; stems flattened and reddish-brown, in ponds, canals and ditches.

species.name: Potamogeton natans
species.tip: Common pondweed with floating, leathery, oval leaves on long stalks with a distinct joint near the blade; also narrow submerged leaves; flower spike held above water.

species.name: Potamogeton perfoliatus
species.tip: Submerged pondweed whose broad, oval, translucent leaves clasp the stem at the base, with no stalks and no floating leaves; in clear, base-rich water.

species.name: Potamogeton polygonifolius
species.tip: Pondweed of acid pools, bog ditches and streams, with oval floating leaves on long stalks that lack the joint seen in Broad-leaved Pondweed; also lance-shaped submerged leaves.

species.name: Potamogeton pusillus
species.tip: Slender, fine submerged pondweed with narrow, linear, three-veined leaves with a blunt or short-pointed tip and no floating leaves; spikes of few widely spaced flowers.

species.name: Potentilla anglica
species.tip: Creeping yellow cinquefoil with stalked leaves of three or five leaflets, flowers with four or five petals, rooting at nodes later; heaths, woods. Compare Tormentil and Creeping Cinquefoil.

species.name: Potentilla anserina
species.tip: Creeping plant with silvery feathery leaves and solitary yellow flowers on long stalks, rooting stolons; trampled grassland, tracks, damp ground.

species.name: Potentilla erecta
species.tip: Slender yellow flower with four petals, unlike other cinquefoils; leaves stalkless with three or five leaflets; heaths, moors, acid grassland.

species.name: Potentilla reptans
species.tip: Long creeping rooting stems; leaves with five stalked leaflets, yellow flowers with five petals; hedgebanks, roadsides, grassland. Compare Trailing Tormentil with fewer leaflets.

species.name: Potentilla sterilis
species.tip: Looks like Wild Strawberry but petals are white with gaps between, the end leaflet tooth shorter, and no fleshy fruit; very early flowers on dry banks and woodland edges.

species.name: Poterium sanguisorba
species.tip: Chalk grassland plant with rounded green-purple flower heads, red stigmas at top and stamens below; leaves of many toothed leaflets, cucumber-scented. Compare Great Burnet, taller with dark red heads.

species.name: Primula veris
species.tip: Nodding one-sided cluster of small deep yellow, scented flowers with tubular calyx on a tall stem from a rosette of wrinkled leaves; grassland, April.

species.name: Primula vulgaris
species.tip: Pale yellow solitary flowers on separate hairy stalks from a rosette of crinkled leaves; woods, banks and hedges in early spring.

species.name: Prunella vulgaris
species.tip: Dense, squarish flower head with purple-tinged bracts and a pair of leaves just below it. Common in lawns.

species.name: Prunus avium
species.tip: Tall tree with white flowers in clusters, glossy red-brown peeling bark with horizontal lines, drooping leaves; fruit red to black. Flowers April, with the new leaves.

species.name: Prunus cerasifera
species.tip: Early white flowers, often before leaves, from February; twigs green and hairless, often thornless; bears round red or yellow plums. Hedges and bushes. Blackthorn flowers later and is thorny.

species.name: Prunus domestica
species.tip: Includes Bullace and Damson; larger oval leaves, downy twigs, flowers white in pairs; fruit bigger than Blackthorn sloes. Hedgerow tree from gardens; sometimes slightly spiny.

species.name: Prunus laurocerasus
species.tip: Large evergreen shrub with big glossy leathery leaves, almond smell when crushed, and upright spikes of small white flowers; black cherry-like fruit. Compare Portugal Laurel with red leaf stalks.

species.name: Prunus lusitanica
species.tip: Evergreen shrub with dark glossy leaves on red stalks, long spikes of fragrant white flowers appearing in summer, later than Cherry Laurel; fruit dark purple.

species.name: Prunus padus
species.tip: Drooping spikes of white almond-scented flowers; leaves oval, finely toothed; black bitter fruit; damp woods, northern England and Scotland. Compare Wild Cherry with clusters not spikes.

species.name: Prunus spinosa
species.tip: Spiny black-barked thicket shrub with white flowers on bare twigs in early spring; fruit are blue-black sloes. Hawthorn flowers later and has lobed leaves.

species.name: Pseudofumaria lutea
species.tip: Tufted garden escape on old walls and rocks with soft, fern-like blue-green leaves and many tubular yellow flowers; long flowering season.

species.name: Pteridium aquilinum
species.tip: Very tall coarse fern forming dense stands from creeping rhizomes with large triangular fronds, dying brown in autumn; heaths, hillsides and woods.

species.name: Puccinellia distans
species.tip: Grass of saltmarsh and salted road verges with branches bent downwards once flowering has finished; small spikelets and no awns.

species.name: Puccinellia maritima
species.tip: Creeping grass of salt marshes with bluish-green flat or folded leaves and a stiff panicle with spreading branches; no awns.

species.name: Pulicaria dysenterica
species.tip: Hairy plant with wavy-edged, clasping leaves and flat-topped clusters of golden, rather narrow-rayed daisies. Damp meadows, ditches and wet roadsides.

species.name: Pulmonaria officinalis
species.tip: Spotted oval leaves and flowers that change from pink to blue-violet. Garden escape in woods and hedges, flowering early in spring.

species.name: Pulsatilla vulgaris
species.tip: Silky-hairy plant of chalk and limestone grassland with large purple bell flowers in spring, then feathery seed heads.

species.name: Pyracantha coccinea
species.tip: Thorny evergreen with clusters of small white flowers and bright orange or red berries in autumn; walls, hedges and waste ground. Cotoneasters lack thorns.

species.name: Pyrus communis
species.tip: Tree with glossy oval leaves, white flowers with purple anthers, branches sometimes spiny; gritty pear fruit. Apple has hairier leaves and pink-tinged flowers.

species.name: Quercus cerris
species.tip: Oak with bristly acorn cups and narrow pointed lobed leaves, rough on the surface; planted tree in parks, spreading in the south.

species.name: Quercus ilex
species.tip: Evergreen oak with dark leathery leaves white-felted beneath, often spiny when young; widely planted and naturalised near coasts.

species.name: Quercus petraea
species.tip: Oak with long-stalked leaves and stalkless acorns; leaf base wedge-shaped with star-hairs on veins beneath; mainly western upland woods.

species.name: Quercus robur
species.tip: Oak with stalked acorns on long stems and almost stalkless leaves with small ear-like lobes at base; common in lowland woods and hedges.

species.name: Quercus rubra
species.tip: Planted oak with large leaves having pointed bristle-tipped lobes, turning red in autumn; acorn cups flat and shallow.

species.name: Ranunculus acris
species.tip: Tall and hairy with no runners; leaves deeply cut like a hand; flower stalks round and smooth, not furrowed.

species.name: Ranunculus aquatilis
species.tip: White flowers on the water; both floating lobed leaves and submerged thread-like leaves; ponds and ditches. Water-crowfoots are a tricky group: check with a specialist.

species.name: Ranunculus arvensis
species.tip: Rare cornfield weed with pale yellow flowers and large seeds covered in sharp spines.

species.name: Ranunculus auricomus
species.tip: Woodland buttercup whose petals are often missing or misshapen; rounded basal leaves, narrow finger-like stem leaves.

species.name: Ranunculus baudotii
species.tip: Water-crowfoot of brackish coastal ditches and pools; floating and thread-like leaves.

species.name: Ranunculus bulbosus
species.tip: Sepals folded right back down the flower stalk; stem base swollen like a small bulb; dry grassland.

species.name: Ranunculus circinatus
species.tip: Stiff, flat, circular fans of short thread-like leaves that keep their shape when lifted out of water.

species.name: Ranunculus flammula
species.tip: Narrow, spear-shaped leaves and small yellow buttercup flowers; wet ground and pond edges.

species.name: Ranunculus fluitans
species.tip: Very long, dark green, tassel-like submerged leaves in fast rivers; no floating leaves.

species.name: Ranunculus hederaceus
species.tip: Small creeping plant of shallow water and mud with only ivy-shaped leaves (no thread-like ones) and tiny white flowers.

species.name: Ranunculus lingua
species.tip: Tall water-edge plant with long narrow leaves and large (3 to 5 cm) yellow flowers.

species.name: Ranunculus omiophyllus
species.tip: Like Ivy-leaved Crowfoot but leaves more deeply lobed and flowers larger; western, on acid mud and in streams.

species.name: Ranunculus ophioglossifolius
species.tip: Very rare; oval to heart-shaped lower leaves and small pale yellow flowers in muddy pools.

species.name: Ranunculus parviflorus
species.tip: Sprawling hairy annual with tiny yellow flowers and rounded, lobed leaves; seeds covered in hooked bumps.

species.name: Ranunculus peltatus
species.tip: Floating rounded leaves plus thread-like submerged ones; large white flowers; ponds and slow water.

species.name: Ranunculus penicillatus
species.tip: Long trailing submerged threads in flowing rivers, sometimes with floating leaves; large white flowers.

species.name: Ranunculus repens
species.tip: Long runners that root at the joints; leaves with three leaflets, the middle one on its own stalk; flower stalks furrowed.

species.name: Ranunculus reptans
species.tip: Very rare; slender arching runners that root at each joint, with narrow leaves; stony lake shores.

species.name: Ranunculus sardous
species.tip: Like Bulbous Buttercup (sepals bent back) but paler yellow, hairier and with no swollen stem base; damp ground, often near the coast.

species.name: Ranunculus sceleratus
species.tip: Hairless, shiny, often hollow stem; tiny pale yellow flowers with a large green fruiting head in the middle; muddy pond edges.

species.name: Ranunculus trichophyllus
species.tip: Only short, submerged thread-like leaves that collapse out of water; small white flowers; ponds and ditches.

species.name: Ranunculus tripartitus
species.tip: Rare, south-west; tiny white flowers; deeply three-lobed floating leaves, sometimes thread-like ones too; seasonal pools.

species.name: Raphanus raphanistrum
species.tip: Yellow, white or lilac flowers with dark veins and long beaded pods constricted between seeds; bristly arable weed with lobed leaves.

species.name: Reseda lutea
species.tip: Biennial or perennial with deeply cut leaves and dense spikes of small pale yellow flowers; chalk and disturbed ground, unlike the undivided leaves of Weld.

species.name: Reseda luteola
species.tip: Tall biennial with a basal rosette and narrow undivided wavy-edged leaves; long slender spikes of small yellowish-green flowers on waste ground.

species.name: Reynoutria japonica
species.tip: Dense thickets of zigzag, bamboo-like red-speckled stems with broad leaves cut straight across at the base; sprays of creamy flowers in autumn.

species.name: Rhamnus cathartica
species.tip: Often thorn-tipped shrub with finely toothed oval leaves in curved veins, opposite buds and black berries; on chalk and limestone scrub, unlike thornless Alder Buckthorn.

species.name: Rhinanthus minor
